title: The Alchemists Formulary
raw_text:
The Alchemist's Formulary



Healers' Recipes

Healers should all know the recipes for the following popular potions. Fortunately, in most cases, the ingredients are common and cheaply obtained.

To restore health to the afflicted and wounded, combine in equal parts two or more of the following cheap and common ingredients: marshmerrow, wickwheat, corkbulb root, and saltrice. Marshmerrow is an important crop of the Ascadian Isles, but it also grows wild in the Grazelands and on Azura's Coast. Wickwheat is a wild Ashland grain that grows in the Grazelands. Corkbulb grows best in the Ascadian Isles. Most saltrice comes from southeastern Morrowind, but there are also some new and prospering farms and plantations in the Ascadian Isles. Saltrice occasionally grows wild in the Grazelands and on Azura's Coast.

To restore fatigue after heavy exertion, combine two or more of the following: crab meat, bread, small kwama egg, and chokeweed. Crabmeat is taken from the mud crab, commonly found along all coasts. Bread in Morrowind is usually baked from saltrice flour. Kwama eggs are harvested from egg mines, and sold everywhere in Morrowind; the smaller eggs retain properties lost in later states of gestation. Chokeweed is a tough shrub growing in the rocky highlands of the West Gash.

To cure common diseases, combine gravedust and green lichen. Gravedust is spirit-affinitive dust taken from remains buried in consecrated ground. Green lichen is a hardy primitive plant that grows in the Ascadian Isles and Azura's Coast.

To restore magicka for spellcasting, combine comberry and frost salts. Comberry is a bitter berry, used to make wines. It grows mainly in the Ascadian Isles. Frost salts, by contrast, are rare and expensive. These crystalline compounds precipitate from elemental frost in solution. Such residues may be collected from the remains of frost atronachs that have been banished from the mortal plane.


Travelers' Recipes

Pilgrims and travelers will find the following inexpensive recipes of particular interest.

Feather reduces the weary traveler's burdens and can be gained from heather and scuttle. Heather is a low evergreen shrub of the Ascadian Isles, known for its small, pinkish-purple flowers. Scuttle, Vvardenfell's favorite local dish, is similar to cheese and made from the flesh of local beetles.

Levitation can be produced from any two of the following ingredients: trama root, racer plumes, and coda flowers. A thick, bitter-tasting root of the trama shrub grows in the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and Red Mountain regions. Racer plumes are plucked from dead cliff racers. Coda flowers are collected from the primitive draggle-tail plant of the Bitter Coast.

The power of Water Breathing is handy for travelers. A potion may be made from two or more of the following ingredients: luminous russula, hackle-lo leaf, and kwama cuttle. Luminous russula is a squat, mottled-brown-and-green toadstool mushroom of the Bitter Coast region. Hackle-lo leaf is a succulent leaf of the Grazelands, prized for its taste and its roborative powers. Kwama cuttle is a tough, waxy substance that comes from sacs in the mouths of kwama.


Adventurers' Recipes

Unfortunately, the potions most favored by adventurers require more rare and expensive ingredients. There are exceptions, like the easy and affordable recipe for fire shield. But most such potions require at least one ingredient with high cost in coin or blood.

Fire Shield potions can be made from comberry and sload soap. Comberry is the bitter berry of the Ascadian Isles. Sload soap is a waxy substance made from the immature non-sentient forms of the sload. Sload soap is not expensive, but is only rarely stocked by apothecaries or alchemists, and cannot be collected locally.

An adventurer can fortify his strength with a potion made from ash yams and dreugh wax. Ash yam is a tough tuberous root vegetable common to the Ascadian Isles region. Dreugh wax is a tough, waxy substance scraped from dreugh shells. Dreugh are powerful aquatic creatures, and hunting them for their hides and wax is a dangerous occupation.

Invisibility, one of the most prized effects of potions, can be made only from crushed diamonds and bittergreen petals. Bittergreen is a red flowering plant growing in the Red Mountain region. Diamonds, on the other hand, are very rare and expensive and usually must be purchased from fine alchemists.

title: Last Words of the Keepers
raw_text:
I am Nulan, Keeper of the Lantern of Udok, and I will speak for both myself and my colleague, for he is Broken and cannot write or speak in a language we understand.



We have always been men of faith, and we have always believed. We believed that when our Clockwork King built His Regent, it would watch over us, and protect us, for it is the heart and mind of the city now. But we know that the Regent, though powerful and all-seeing, is a machine. And machines can become Broken. And when the Regent Broke, so went the rest of the city. And now we sit here, stranded in a metal tower in the middle of a sea as the world falls to pieces around us. And we wonder if faith really meant that much.

We believed that He and His Regent placed us here. We believed that we were forever marooned in this oil ocean, to watch over it, and we believed that there was no way to cross such a vast expanse. But we know that underneath this lighthouse, in the core, its very bones, hold the secret to crossing the Valley of Udok.

We believed that the Regent and Seht would save us from the destruction of their city, and that if we remain here our faith shall be rewarded. Be we know if we stay here, we will die.

title: Transmeta Interivatives
How Two Moon
raw_text:
HOW TWO MOON BY ANDY



...I hypothesize, based on de-encoded Dreamsleeve memospores intended for the thrice-forsaken House Wizards of the varliance-rend, that, with high probability, it may be possible to re-enact the traumatic birth of this world without, as it were, the trauma. By reversing the failure of the C-signs, Pigmius in particular, through use not of padhomaic nor draconid-wrought thaumaturgy, but rather through the metals and machinations of Our Lord, we avoid the drama caused by personality and the violence of self. We avoid both the Scarab and the Scarab-framer, don't you see? They intended it to the thus! They were created, they create, and we created them in return! And now we create anew a perfect clockwork world, drifting through Oblivion, unmarred by fleshy imperfection....

title: Vehk's First Poem
raw_text: For you, I would shave this head. It would not do that your new friend shook an inconstant kwam-lice from it. I'd take the sigil of Vel, the V, and wear it twice. And I would be new, and believe in the one moon and star as your banner does. I’d make a legend of this netch longhook. Make no frown that this will be my weapon in your guard, however low its station. We all drink from the milk of our fathers. I’d learn to read and then write so that I could see right your name forever. And I would clean your feet so that the next time you made treaty it would be with an assured step.

title: Musings on Power
raw_text:
[This is a collection of mutterings of the High Foremer, as recorded by his scribe Alammu 73912]



Power. Energy. Materiality in potentia, daedronics, however you want to describe it. That which allows motion, the agent of change. Only made possible by the intermingling of Anu and Padomay, Change and Stasis, IS and IS NOT. Exists infinitely but unusable in Aetherius, spiralling constantly towards entropy in Oblivion. All that is in the Grey Maybe requires some form of it, and the sources are myriad. Magnus. AnuLorkhan. Mundane kinesis.

It requires power to move power. The further away something is from the source, the harder it is to move power there and the more you lose along the way. It's slippery. Always jumping. Always wants to escape. Except dracochrysalids, but those require more power to produce than you can possibly get and aren't very useful anyways. Religious experiment. Idiot Saliache keep trying.

When building infrastructure, build close to power. Less waste. Efficient. Great construction requires enormous power. And if the power dies, the closest and the greatest are the first and worst affected. Fundamental axiom. In magic, in politics, in theosophy. No-one seems to notice. No-one seems to learn.

title: Call to Arms
raw_text:
TO MY FELLOW CITIZENS OF SOTHA SIL.

The vile calumnies uttered against us by the contemptable residents of the low side of the wall have gone too far! They slander us! They attempt to browbeat us! The accuse us of laziness, shiftlessness, intellectual dishonesty, and sins too great and too vile to be again repeated! Not three photic cycles ago, a man in rags had the gall, the sheer temerity, to spark at me. Spark at me!
My fellow thinking fabricants, I say, Enough! I have tolerated their villifications long enough! We have used words, and words have won us nothing. Discourse has failed. Debate has failed. They do not apologize, they do not repent, and, worst of all, they deny that they have comitted any wrongdoing at all! Shameful! Detestable!
My fellow citizens, we must take action! We must march, and let them know, let them truly know, how through their own actions they have brought down this violence upon themselves. We have watched, and seen treachery. We have wondered, to no avail. And what little rapport between us was once built up, we must now tear down.
Yours in Seht, Retharus 43276

title: De Rerum Mutabilitatis
raw_text:
De Rerum Mutabilitatis
by Quintus Sextus Septus VIII



I write this treatise in honor and mourning of the death of the last known Mimic, hacked to pieces by an irate adventurer who found that the door he was opening led to a closet filled with gnashing teeth rather than the handful of Sepetims he was presumably expecting. It is a great blow to the academic community, given that mimics were unique in their ability to shift forms at will and their willingness to remain stationary for extended periods.

Created by a mad Chimeri wizard some time in the first two centuries of the First Era, mimics were designed to be the perfect guardians of the treasure troves that old mages inevitably seem to collect. However, they were an odd blend of flesh and metal the likes of which Nirn had never before seen, nor would ever see again. Because of their artificial creation, there was a finite number of them, though over the centuries they disseminated throughout northern Tamriel, ranging from Morrowind to High Rock.

They would typically find for themselves a disused room and take on a form alluring to people rummaging about, blending well with the surrounding environs. They did not actually require sustenance, but seemed to relish feasting on the unwary regardless, most probably because their creator had a twisted sense of humor.

title: Notes on the Clocktower
raw_text:
The Tower. Everyone sees it, nobody thinks about it. It's just there. It dominates the city. Sun, moons. Makes them. Illusion? Probably. Something else? Possibly, possibly. Enormous power, that's for sure, whether illusion or not. The Tower's the key, I know that much. All that energy. Wasted. Wasted! On some pretty lights! It's not as though we're wanting for clocks here. Not as though we need one more, not one as big and useless as that. Such inefficiency. Such inefficiency! How could our Lord devise something so useless?

Obvious, then. God is perfect from every angle to behold. Poetic nonsense, but true enough. Lord Sotha did not create it personally, as he did not personally create everything in this city. Underling. Stupid. Utter idiot. Wasting power on a vanity project. Surprised the Foremer stands for it, hates inefficiency as much as I do. Maybe he doesn't even know. Not as though he ever goes outside the foundry. Hrah.

I've got to get in, then. Look around a bit. See what makes it tick. Cut the power. End it. We can use lamps. We have those. Same with clocks. No loss. Safe. I'll redirect the power to some place that needs it. Arboretum? Maybe. Foundry? Maybe. Why not both? They'll call me a useful and efficacious mer after they see what I've done.

Got to get to work.

I'll redirect the power to some place that needs it. Arboretum? Maybe. Foundry? Maybe. Why not both? They'll call me a useful and efficacious mer after they see what I've done.

Got to get to work.
